findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — [P1, confidence 100] `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` builds the calendar client from the caller even though attendees are authorized callers, so an attendee-triggered addition updates calendars through the attendee's credentials instead of the booking organizer credentials already loaded with `booking.user`, targeting the wrong integration or failing to update the organizer's event.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — [P1, confidence 100] `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` runs only after `prisma.booking.update` has committed the new attendees, so a calendar-provider rejection leaves the database changed while the API fails and every retry hits `uniqueGuests.length === 0`, permanently stranding the external event with a stale attendee list.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124 — [P1, confidence 100] `const evt: CalendarEvent = {` constructs the notification event without `team` after loading only `eventType: true`, so `sendAddGuestsEmails` always sees `calendarEvent.team?.members` as absent and silently omits organizer notifications to every team member.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70 — [P1, confidence 100] `process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())` normalizes only the blacklist while line 77 compares the raw guest, so an uppercase variant of a blacklisted address bypasses the policy and is persisted as an attendee.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — [P2, confidence 100] `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(` checks requested addresses against the pre-write attendee snapshot without canonicalizing case or enforcing uniqueness within `guests`, so case variants and repeated addresses represent one mailbox as multiple attendees and concurrent calls race past the same check before insertion.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — [P2, confidence 100] `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` passes the unfiltered request rather than the inserted `uniqueGuests`, so an input mixing an existing attendee with a new address classifies that existing attendee as newly added and sends the scheduled-event email instead of the guest-list-change email.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — [P2 advisory, confidence 100] `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` accepts an unbounded collection that is eagerly inserted, translated, rendered, and dispatched with `Promise.all`; even if the UI normally adds a few rows, a direct authenticated caller makes one request materialize and fan out across arbitrarily many guests, so adding a schema maximum deletes the need to trust every caller and prevents a request-sized scalability cliff.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the schema at line 5 of addGuests.schema.ts defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` without any maximum length constraint. Looking at the handler in addGuests.handler.ts, the guests array is processed through: 1) database insertion via createMany, 2) translation lookups for each attendee, 3) email sending via Promise.all in sendAddGuestsEmails. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that blacklistedGuestEmails is normalized to lowercase via `.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())` on line 68-70, but the guest emails from input are compared directly without normalization in the filter on line 74. This means a guest email like 'BLOCKED@example.com' would not match 'blocked@example.com' in the blacklist. Similarly, the comparison with existing attendees (`guest === attendee.email`) doesn't normalize either side, so 'USER@example.com' wouldn't match 'user@example.com'. This is a real correctness bug that allows bypassing the blacklist and duplicate checks.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that authorization check at line 59 allows any attendee (isAttendee) to add guests to a booking. The code explicitly permits this: `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) { throw new TRPCError... }`. This means any attendee can add arbitrary email addresses as guests, triggering calendar invitations with full event details to those addresses. This is a security concern as attendees typically shouldn't have permission to modify bookings by adding new participants - this should be restricted to organizers or team admins. The finding correctly identifies this as a potential security/authorization issue.
